programme: No recognizable single module. The list mixes lineage-defining homeodomain/LIM-homeodomain master regulators from mutually unrelated organs — NKX2-5 (cardiac), TTF1/NKX2-1 (thyroid/lung), ISL1 (pancreatic islet/motor neuron), DLX4, ALX3 and NR2F1 (neural crest/craniofacial), ATOH1 (inner ear/sensory neuron), HOXA10 (uterus/limb) — together with a SWI/SNF (BAF) subunit (SMARCC1), a MAPK-responsive ETS factor (ELK1), a muscle-differentiation MADS-box factor (MEF2A) and a generic transcriptional coactivator (CREBBP). Beyond the trivial fact that CREBBP/EP300-class coactivators and BAF-class remodelers are recruited by essentially all sequence-specific developmental TFs, these factors share no common target program, signalling pathway, or physical complex that can be named from the list itself.
role_in_a: Not established — none of these factors has a recorded Open Targets association or retrieved literature link to fibromyalgia, and blood is not the tissue in which any of them (cardiac, thyroid, islet, neural-crest, otic, uterine identity factors) is expected to act.
role_in_b: Not established — none of these factors has a recorded Open Targets association or retrieved literature link to psoriasis, and skin is likewise not the expected site of activity for this set of organ-identity regulators.
shared_axis: No defensible shared axis can be constructed. If anything connects the two lists it is that both are residual developmental/organ-identity transcription factors left after tissue-generic immune and proliferation regulators (STAT1, STAT3, SPI1, TCF7, EZH2, etc.) were stripped out as too common to blood and skin — which argues these hits are the low-signal tail of the concordance ranking rather than a biological module shared by the two diseases.
reasoning: The twelve factors span at least seven unrelated developmental lineages plus a chromatin remodeler, a MAPK effector and a general coactivator, with no common pathway, complex, or target logic connecting them; this is a list of co-occurring names, not a mechanism. Every factor shows no Open Targets association in either disease and essentially no retrievable literature (the single HOXA10 hit concerns endometriosis and is explicitly flagged as unclear relevance to fibromyalgia), so there is nothing in the record to anchor a story even if one were invented.
how_to_falsify: Take the strongest-recurring candidates (SMARCC1, ALX3, ISL1 at 24-26/32) and test in relevant primary cells (PBMCs/blood leukocytes for fibromyalgia, keratinocytes for psoriasis) whether they are even expressed and whether ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq shows them occupying the listed target promoters in that tissue; if these organ-identity factors are not expressed or bound in blood or skin at all, the concordance is a network-inference artifact rather than shared disease biology, which is the expected outcome given the current record.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (fibromyalgia) vs skin (psoriasis), neither of which is the native tissue for any of the developmental factors listed. The 32 patient-group comparisons rest on only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the recurrence counts are not 32 independent replications and should be read with that pseudo-replication in mind. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed the immune/proliferation factors most plausible for a blood-skin inflammatory link (STAT1, STAT3, SPI1, TCF7, EZH2, BCL6, AR), which is consistent with what remains being non-specific rather than a hidden shared programme.
